skill.name: git-advanced
skill.description: Advanced Git workflow guidance for rebasing, conflict resolution, bisecting, branch cleanup, reflog recovery, and safe history rewriting.
skill.summary: Guide advanced Git operations with safety-focused workflows and recovery steps.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown command examples, placeholder URLs, and Git troubleshooting snippets. The executable helper script does run local Git commands that can modify repository state, so users should review it before execution, but no evidence of malicious intent, credential exfiltration, prompt injection, or unauthorized network behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Executable helper script can modify local repository state.
remediation.suggestion: Document that scripts/git_helper.sh should be reviewed before execution and run only in the intended repository.

remediation.issue: Branch cleanup examples use xargs with Git branch names.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer safer loops with quoted branch names and explicit allowlists for protected branches.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting documentation references SSH private key paths.
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that users should only add their own keys and should never paste or share private key contents.

content.value_statement: Complex Git history and conflicts can slow teams and risk lost work. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code structured workflows for rebasing, recovery, branch cleanup, and conflict resolution.
actual_capabilities: Explains interactive rebase workflows for squashing, reordering, editing, and dropping commits.
Guides merge conflict resolution using ours, theirs, manual editing, and merge tools.
Provides Git bisect steps for manual and automated regression hunting.
Documents reflog recovery techniques for lost commits, bad resets, and deleted branches.
Includes branch strategy guidance for Git Flow, trunk-based development, releases, and hotfixes.
Provides a shell helper script for branch cleanup, conflict assistance, history viewing, and stash management.
limitations: It cannot guarantee recovery after garbage collection or expired reflog entries.
Some workflows can rewrite history and require user judgment before running commands.
The helper script operates on the current local repository and should be reviewed before execution.
Examples use placeholder repositories, branches, and file names that users must adapt.

use_cases.title: Clean a feature branch before review
use_cases.description: Use interactive rebase guidance to squash work-in-progress commits and present a clear commit history.

use_cases.title: Recover from a destructive Git mistake
use_cases.description: Use reflog and recovery workflows to restore lost commits, deleted branches, or a pre-reset state.

use_cases.title: Standardize team branching practices
use_cases.description: Compare Git Flow, trunk-based development, feature branches, releases, and hotfix workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Resolve my current merge conflict
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me understand my Git merge conflict. Explain what ours and theirs mean, then give safe next steps before I stage files.

prompt_templates.title: Clean up my branch history
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me prepare an interactive rebase plan for my last commits. I want a clean review history without losing work.

prompt_templates.title: Find when a bug was introduced
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through using git bisect to find the commit that introduced a regression. Include manual and automated options.

prompt_templates.title: Recover lost Git work safely
prompt_templates.prompt: I may have lost commits after a reset or rebase. Help me use reflog and recovery branches before I run destructive commands.

output_examples.input: I have five messy commits and need a clean pull request.
output: Claude suggests creating a backup branch first.
Claude maps each commit to pick, squash, fixup, or reword.
Claude warns not to rebase commits already shared with teammates.
Claude helps identify the last good commit.
Claude recommends recreating the branch before trying more destructive recovery steps.

output_examples.input: We need a release branch workflow.
output: Claude compares Git Flow and trunk-based options.
Claude outlines branch names and merge points.
Claude highlights where hotfixes and release stabilization fit.

best_practices: Create a backup branch before any rebase, reset, cleanup, or history rewrite.
Use force-with-lease instead of force push, and avoid rewriting shared branch history.
Read helper scripts and run Git status before executing commands that change branches or files.
anti_patterns: Do not run cleanup commands blindly on repositories with important unmerged branches.
Do not resolve conflicts by choosing one side without understanding both changes.
Do not rely on reflog recovery as a substitute for backups and remote pushes.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands automatically?
faq.answer: The skill provides guidance and includes a helper script. Users should review commands before execution.

faq.question: Is it safe for shared branches?
faq.answer: It includes warnings about shared history. Rebase and force push guidance should be used only with team agreement.

faq.question: Can it recover every lost commit?
faq.answer: No. Recovery depends on reflog entries, object retention, and whether Git garbage collection removed unreachable objects.

faq.question: What Git topics does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers rebasing, conflicts, bisect, cherry-pick, reflog recovery, branch strategies, cleanup, and troubleshooting.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Developers, tech leads, and release managers who already use Git and need safer advanced workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace Git documentation?
faq.answer: No. It organizes common workflows and examples, but users should still verify commands for their repository.
